Tone: Solid growth and low unemployment are positives, but “somewhat elevated” inflation keeps policy restrictive. By holding the funds rate at 4.25–4.5% and continuing balance-sheet runoff, the stance aligns with Taylor-type prescriptions under inflation above target and output near potential (Taylor; Clarida–Galí–Gertler). The emphasis on “balanced risks” and data dependence is consistent with the real-time uncertainty literature (Orphanides), while continued QT and operational settings (IORB, standing facilities) reflect modern corridor/floor operating procedures (Goodfriend) and could modestly lift term premia per yield-curve evidence (Cochrane; Piazzesi). Overall, the communication is cautiously neutral with a slight positive tilt from steady policy and balanced-risk language, tempered by ongoing QT and acknowledgment of elevated inflation.
